title: The longer version
intro: The resume is the summary. This page is where I keep the story behind it: how I got into infrastructure, what I believe about running platforms, and what I am building in the lab right now.

sections.heading: How I got here
paragraphs: I started on a help desk, moved to a NOC, and spent a few years as a sysadmin before the first Kubernetes cluster landed on my desk. Every step was the same lesson: the system that is easiest to explain is the one that stays up.
These days I lead a platform group. The job is less about typing YAML and more about making the paved road the obvious choice for forty other engineers.

sections.heading: What I believe
bullets: Everything is a pull request. If it is not in git, it is not real.
Alerts page for symptoms, not causes. Dashboards exist so people open them.
Blameless post-mortems, written down, acted on.
The platform team's customers are engineers. Treat them like customers.

sections.heading: In the lab
paragraphs: This site runs on the same home lab I use to try things before they reach work: Talos nodes on bare metal, Argo CD for delivery, OpenTelemetry for the signals. The lab is where I break things on purpose.
